title: What to Watch This Week: Samantha’s ₹100 Crore Hit Finally Streams, and Margot Robbie Haunts the Moors
excerpt: From a Telugu assassin-housewife blockbuster to Emerald Fennell’s Wuthering Heights, plus Will Ferrell on the golf course and the final chapter of Heartstopper — your streaming calendar from July 13 to 19.
body:
Some weeks, the streaming gods are generous. This is one of those weeks. Between a Telugu blockbuster that shattered records, an Emerald Fennell literary adaptation starring two of the most photogenic humans alive, and Will Ferrell doing what he does best in spandex on a golf course, the July 13–19 window is stacked. Here are seven picks, ranked by how quickly you should cancel your plans.

## 1. Maa Inti Bangaaram — JioHotstar, July 17

**Samantha Ruth Prabhu** is a docile daughter-in-law. Except she’s actually a retired assassin and former Naxalite rebel named Jhansi. When her psychotic ex-gang leader tracks her down at a family wedding in a conservative village, the sari comes off and the bloodshed begins.

If that pitch doesn’t hook you, the numbers will. *Maa Inti Bangaaram* became the highest-grossing solo female-led Telugu film of all time during its theatrical run, crossing ₹100 crore with an ease that stunned even the trade. Directed by **B.V. Nandini Reddy** with a ferocious Samantha at its centre and **Gulshan Devaiah** chewing scenery as the villain, this is part family comedy, part John Wick, and entirely irresistible. The fact that Samantha reportedly shot portions of the film while battling morning sickness only adds to the legend.

**Where to watch in the US/UK/Canada:** JioHotstar — available in Telugu with dubbed versions.

## 2. Wuthering Heights — JioHotstar, July 13 (Already streaming)

**Emerald Fennell** directing **Margot Robbie** and **Jacob Elordi** on the Yorkshire moors is the kind of sentence that makes you sit up. The *Saltburn* director brings her signature eye for beauty-laced cruelty to Emily Brontë’s Heathcliff and Catherine — and the casting is inspired. Elordi has the brooding, feral magnetism the role demands, and Robbie brings a wildness to Catherine that feels genuinely dangerous rather than decoratively tragic.

Look out for **Shazad Latif** in a supporting role — the British-Pakistani actor continues to build one of the most interesting careers in prestige cinema. With **Hong Chau** also in the ensemble, this isn’t just another period piece. Fennell doesn’t do “just another” anything.

**Where to watch:** JioHotstar.

## 3. Raktanchal Season 3 — Prime Video & MX Player, July 16

The gang wars of Purvanchal move to the state assembly in Lucknow, and somehow get even bloodier. **Kranti Prakash Jha** returns as Vijay Singh, now attempting to go legit through politics, while **Nikitin Dheer’s** Waseem Khan builds lethal new alliances to destroy him. Add **Mahie Gill** and **Karan Patel** to the mix, and you have a Hindi crime drama that’s never heard of subtlety — and is better for it.

The first two seasons built a loyal cult following with their raw, unflinching depiction of UP’s criminal-political nexus. Season 3 promises to be the biggest yet. Stream it for free on MX Player if you don’t have Prime.

**Where to watch:** Prime Video (subscription) or MX Player (free).

## 4. The Hawk — Netflix, July 16

**Will Ferrell** as a washed-up golf prodigy trying to complete the Grand Slam while his entire dysfunctional family rides along? With **Willem Dafoe** and **Jane Lynch** in supporting roles? Directed by the *Jury Duty* team? This has sleeper-hit energy written all over it.

Ferrell hasn’t had a streaming vehicle this well-positioned in years, and the early buzz suggests *The Hawk* finds the sweet spot between absurdist comedy and genuine family drama. Think *Talladega Nights* meets *The Bear*, but on a fairway.

**Where to watch:** Netflix.

## 5. Heartstopper Forever — Netflix, July 17

The final chapter of Alice Oseman’s beloved YA series arrives, and if you’ve been following Nick and Charlie since season one, bring tissues. **Kit Connor** and **Joe Locke** face the one thing scarier than coming out: growing apart. University looms, long-distance threatens, and their circle of friends navigates the bittersweet business of moving on.

*Heartstopper* has always been the gentlest show on television — warm, affirming, and quietly radical in its normalisation of queer joy. The finale promises to honour that legacy while acknowledging that first love doesn’t always survive adulthood. It’s going to wreck you, beautifully.

**Where to watch:** Netflix.

## 6. Ride or Die — Prime Video, July 15 (Already streaming)

**Octavia Spencer** discovers her best friend **Hannah Waddingham** is secretly a deadly international assassin. A botched hit sends them on a chaotic sprint across Europe, dodging killers, Interpol, and their own spectacular dysfunction. **Bill Nighy** and **Ed Skrein** round out a cast that has no business being this stacked for a summer action-comedy.

It’s breezy, violent, and very funny — the kind of movie that exists to be watched on a Friday night with a glass of wine and zero expectations. Sometimes that’s exactly what you need.

**Where to watch:** Prime Video.

## 7. Ready or Not 2: Here I Come — JioHotstar, July 16

**Samara Weaving** returns for round two of the horror franchise that made hide-and-seek genuinely terrifying. This time, rival occult dynasties and a surprise sister (**Kathryn Newton**) raise the stakes, with **Sarah Michelle Gellar** joining the chaos. If the first film was a savage eat-the-rich satire dressed as a slasher, the sequel promises to double down on both the satire and the body count.

**Where to watch:** JioHotstar.

---

**Also arriving this week:** *Second Love*, a Tamil dating reality show hosted by Ramya Krishnan (JioHotstar, July 13); *Pavithram Season 2*, a Malayalam family drama (JioHotstar, July 13); *Spooky in Love*, a Korean supernatural rom-com starring Park Eun-bin (Netflix, July 18); and *The East Palace*, a dark fantasy K-drama with Nam Joo-hyuk (Netflix, July 17).

*Happy watching. Your couch will understand.*
